title: Three churches and a market
ring: City L · Grote Markt · three Gothic churches · the Weeuwhof · {{KM}} km ·
sub: Into Poperinge by Werf, out by Kleine Casseldreef; the old town in between.
desc: A {{KM}} km walk from Kleine Dasdreef into Poperinge: Gasthuisstraat, Grote Markt, Sint-Bertinus, Sint-Jan, Onze-Lieve-Vrouw and the Weeuwhof.

waypoints.name: Home
waypoints.title: Out of the door
waypoints.note: Down the gravel lane to Kleine Dasdreef, then left, up the dreef to Helleketelweg and right, towards town.

waypoints.name: Nine Elms
waypoints.label: Nine Elms
waypoints.title: Past Nine Elms
waypoints.note: A small war cemetery between the fields on Helleketelweg, ten minutes from the door. Worth the two-minute detour through the gate even on a town walk.
waypoints.accent: Most people in Poperinge do not know it is here.

waypoints.name: Hopmuseum
waypoints.label: Hopmuseum
waypoints.title: Gasthuisstraat
waypoints.note: Werf and Duinkerkestraat bring you into the main shopping street. The Hopmuseum is in the old municipal weighing house where the hop bales were weighed and stamped; Talbot House is a few doors on.

waypoints.name: Gasthuiskapel
waypoints.title: The Gasthuiskapel
waypoints.note: At the end of the street, the chapel of the medieval hospital, now an exhibition space; look in if the door is open.

waypoints.name: Grote Markt
waypoints.label: Grote Markt
waypoints.title: Grote Markt and Sint-Bertinus
waypoints.note: The square with the neo-Gothic town hall of 1911 and, behind it, Sint-Bertinuskerk, the main church, with its heavy tower. Cafés all round the square for a coffee.

waypoints.name: Sint-Janskerk
waypoints.label: Sint-Janskerk
waypoints.title: Sint-Janskerk
waypoints.note: East along Bruggestraat to the second Gothic church, home of the miraculous statue of Our Lady of Sint-Jan and of the Maria procession every July.

waypoints.name: Toekomststraat
waypoints.title: South and west through the back streets
waypoints.note: Leave by the quieter streets south of the centre, towards the third church.

waypoints.name: OLV-kerk
waypoints.label: O.L.V.-kerk
waypoints.title: Onze-Lieve-Vrouwekerk
waypoints.note: The oldest of the three, 13th century, a hall church in a green square. The parish outgrew it; it stands quiet now.

waypoints.name: Weeuwhof
waypoints.label: Weeuwhof
waypoints.title: The Weeuwhof
waypoints.note: Through the gate on Sint-Annastraat: a courtyard of small 18th-century almshouses built for widows, still lived in, with benches under the trees.

waypoints.name: Kleine Casseldreef
waypoints.label: Kleine Casseldreef
waypoints.title: Home by Kleine Casseldreef
waypoints.note: Out of town by Provenstraat, then right into Kleine Casseldreef: a long straight lane between the fields, back towards the dreef and the gravel lane.

goodtoknow: Lanes to town, pavement in it. Shops close on Sunday; the churches are usually open in the daytime, the Weeuwhof gate too. Market on Friday mornings on Grote Markt.
Poperinge got its town rights in 1147 and grew rich on cloth, then on hops, which is why the Hopmuseum sits in the old weighing house and why there are three Gothic churches for a town this size.
more: The three churches are the mark of the medieval cloth town: Sint-Bertinus for the centre, Sint-Jan and Onze-Lieve-Vrouw for the parishes that grew around it. Hop growing took over from the 15th century and Poperinge is still the hop capital of Belgium, with the Hoppefeesten every three years in September.
tlcue: Clockwise. Distances are from the front door.
